summary: Democratic Sen. Gary Peters did not seek a third term, so the seat was open. Abdul El-Sayed (Democrat) defeated Mike Rogers (Republican) and other candidates.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.bio: Abdul El-Sayed is a Democrat and epidemiologist who formerly served as a Wayne County health official and ran for Michigan governor in 2018. He won the 2026 Democratic Senate primary over U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens. His campaign centers on Medicare for All.

positions.summary: Says he "literally wrote the book on Medicare for All" and that it does not have to ban additional private insurance through unions or employers.
Says ICE should be abolished and immigration enforcement rebuilt under a new structure, with a safe, secure border and a clear pathway to citizenship for people stuck in limbo.
Says he will tax capital gains over $1 million as ordinary income, tax billionaire wealth, and close the Social Security payroll tax cap.
Says he will raise the minimum teacher salary to at least $60,000, fully fund IDEA, and oppose vouchers.
Says he will create a pathway to 100% renewable energy and codify the EPA's Endangerment Finding into law.

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.bio: Mike Rogers is a Republican who was born and raised in Livingston County, Michigan, served as an Army lieutenant, and worked as an FBI special agent. He represented Michigan in the U.S. House from 2001 to 2015 and chaired the House Intelligence Committee. He lost the 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin by about 19,000 votes.

positions.summary: Says he wants to bring manufacturing jobs back home.
Says hospitals and insurers should have to show real prices before care, wants wider access to Trump Rx bulk drug purchasing, and would require insurers to publish denial rates.
Says he wants to prioritize education, not indoctrination.
Said in a 2024 campaign ad that Michigan voters have already decided the abortion issue, that he respects that decision, and that he would not do anything to change it in the Senate.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35)
